The decisive mistake was in the Orchestrator's initial plan at Step 1. Because "Maktay" means "is pleasing to", the thing doing the liking becomes the direct object, so "I" belongs in the accusative form "Mato". The thing being liked, apples, becomes the subject in the nominative form "Apple". The correct sentence is therefore "Maktay Mato Apple".

The Orchestrator instead used "Zapple" (accusative) for apples and "Mato" for the subject. This reversed the roles and gave "Maktay Zapple Mato". Its own plan also called "Pa" the nominative subject, which contradicted the final construction. The later steps only repeated this wrong answer.
